note: Six primitive camping spots in the loess hills above the Missouri River floodplain, each one a small gravel parking lot (lettered A to G on the area map) with room to camp beside it. Five are in the west tract: two at the foot of the bluff off Route T, both beside a busy railroad line, and three up on the ridge along gravel Quebec Road, where the lot at the road bend near the shooting range has open mown ground next to it. The sixth is the trailhead lot by a fishing pond in the east tract, off Route O; the multi-use trails that start there are open to horses. The river itself is miles off across the floodplain and not in view. No pads, tables or water; the only privy is at the shooting range. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: MDC 'Designated Camping Sites' and 'Individual Campsites' - six Primitive Camping Area symbols on the map, each beside a lettered Parking Lot (A, B, C, D, E, G), and six GIS camping points. Free, FCFS, no hookups, 14-day limit; the brochure limits camping to the areas on the map. Phone matches the area page. Every spot is a lot; none is a built camp. Pin is on lot G beside the railroad; lot E is the most usable - flagged.
flags: INCLUSION (lot rule - stays, all lots): the area page lists 'Camping: Designated Camping Sites' and 'Individual Campsites'; the brochure says 'Primitive camping is permitted only in areas identified on area map. Camping is limited to 14 consecutive days in a 30-day period.' The map (08/10) draws a Primitive Camping Area symbol beside six of its seven lettered parking lots (not F, the shooting-range lot, which has the privy); GIS layer 27 has six 'Primitive Camping Area' points, each 25-45 m from a GIS lot. Each lot carries a designated camping point, so the entry stays under the 2026-11-09 rule. On imagery there is no loop, pad, table or privy at any of the six.

LOTS VERSUS REAL CAMPS (180 m leaf-off frames, dark imagery): G at 39.93487,-95.14771 (stored pin; west tract, off Route T): a gravel spur about 60 m long to a small lot under trees, the point in timber 25 m east; the railroad main line is about 60 m south-west (a train is on it in the frame). B at 39.91844,-95.12425 (off Route T, 2.7 km south-east of G): a gravel turnaround about 20 m across, the railroad about 30 m from it. E at 39.93942,-95.12460 (ridge top, Quebec Road bend, 300 m east of the range): a gravel lot about 20 x 15 m at the road junction with open mown grass south of it; the GIS point is on that grass 30 m from the lot beside a service track. D at 39.93029,-95.11572 and C at 39.92463,-95.11531 (Quebec Road, east side): small lots in timber, C a short loop. A at 39.91925,-95.09144 (east tract, end of the gravel road from Route O): a gravel lot about 25 x 15 m beside Pond 1, the point on a small grass patch 20 m south-east; this is the trailhead of the multi-use trails.

CLUSTERS / SPLIT: west tract - G and B on Route T (2.7 km apart), E, D, C along Quebec Road (0.6-1.7 km apart); east tract - A alone, about 2.9 km east of C by air with its own entrance on Route O. NO SPLIT proposed: A is on its own road but is a single small lot.

PIN: stored 39.93487,-95.14771 = GIS point 265 at lot G, a minor spot beside the railroad. There is no clear main camp. The most usable spot is lot E (open mown ground beside the lot, on the ridge, near the range privy): 39.93974,-95.12489 is the GIS lot, 39.93942,-95.12460 the camping point - about 2.0 km east-north-east of the stored pin. Owner's call whether to move it.

HORSES: the map labels no horse camp. The area page says 'This department area also has multi-use trails open to equestrian use'; on the map the multi-use trails are in the east tract and start at lot A. Lot A is drawn with the same Primitive Camping Area symbol as the others, so it is not distinguished as an equestrian camp; the entry's pin is not on it.

ACCESS: 'To the east tract: from Oregon, take Highway 59 east, then Route O south 3.25 miles to the highway sign. To reach the west tract: continue south on Route O, then take Route T west 1.50 miles to the area.' The map legend shows Routes O and T paved and Quebec Road, road 310 and the spur to lot A as Gravel Road. No low-water crossing, 4WD wording or posted limit on the page, brochure or map. OSM was unread (the Overpass mirror timed out).

WATERFRONT: stored not waterfront stands - the area page describes 'loess hill river bluffs overlooking the Missouri River floodplain'; the river is several miles away and none of the lots is on water except lot A beside Pond 1, a small fishing pond (ponds do not count).
PHONE: stored 816-271-3100 matches the area page's 'For more information call (816) 271-3100'.
SEASON: stored year_round (manual) stands; the brochure gives no camping season (the multi-use trails close for firearms deer and spring turkey seasons).
